# `acknowledgement-expired`

An acknowledgement expired

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `acknowledgement-expired` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M6) |
| **Group** | Spec and engine notices ([RULES.md section 11](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An acknowledgement's `expires` date has passed (as of today, or `--as-of`), so its finding counts again and can fail CI.

## Why this default

Notice only: it explains why a previously accepted finding is back.

## Example

From test case [`acknowledgement-expired`](../../test/cases/acknowledgement-expired/): The acknowledgement expired on 2026-11-01 (as of 2026-11-21): acknowledgement-expired (info) explains why the removal counts again and fails CI.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
-   '/pets/{id}':
-     delete:
-       responses:
-         '200':
-           description: ok
```

Findings:

- `operation-removed` · error · DELETE /pets/{id}
- `acknowledgement-expired` · info · DELETE /pets/{id}

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  acknowledgement-expired: info
```

## How to fix

Fix the change, or renew the acknowledgement with a new `expires` date and reason.
